question: How to implement logistic regression with the specified gradient descent conventions and analyze regularization, interaction features, and model compression?
alternatives: Implement custom gradient descent following exact specification
Use automatic differentiation library with custom training loop
rationale: The task specifies exact gradient descent conventions (200 iterations, lr=0.1, clipping, specific update rule) that differ from standard solvers. Custom implementation ensures reproducibility and adherence to the exact specification. This is necessary because the reference answer follows this exact trajectory.
decision: Implement custom full-batch gradient descent trainer with exact conventions: 200 iterations, learning rate 0.1, logit clipping [-30, 30], weights/bias initialized at 0, and specified update rule with L2 regularization.
expected_effect: Consistent reproducible results matching reference implementation. 5-fold CV will identify optimal lambda. Paired t-test will quantify interaction feature utility. Compression analysis will identify best sparsity-quantization trade-off.
falsifier: If results diverge from expected convergence patterns or if fold cross-validation produces illogical ordering of lambda performance, the implementation may be incorrect and requires debugging.
